title: Check changes against cited documents; bar self-marked covered rows
summary: The verifier prompt gains a rule: when the request cites a document, compare the change with it, and falling short is a request-reading mismatch, which is major. The producer prompt gains a rule that a job may not mark its own requirement rows Covered. Rows A9-1 and A10-1 in the requirements map go back to Partial with the reasons. The audience is the user, who judges whether Athena's verdicts can be trusted.

defaults_applied.how: The cause is that the verifier prompt never compares the change with a cited document, and that a job can mark its own rows. Both are closed as rules, not by fixing only the one job.
The new rules are enforced through the existing request_reading_mismatch to major path in judge(). Anything still prose-only is marked so.
The map reasons and the decision entry cite BRIEF.md rows and job 20261014-174815-7bf8.
One focused change to prompts and docs, with no new code.
The budgets test and the workspace tests, clippy and fmt must pass.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: The steward's missing model call is the reason A9-1 is Partial. I did not read steward.rs, so the producer must confirm this against the code before writing the reason.
The fix is prompt rules plus the map correction. A new code check (for example, one that scans a diff for rows turned Covered) is not required by the request, so the producer need not build one.

The verifier prompt budget is 1,300 tokens and it currently uses about 1,148 (D93), so a few dozen added tokens fit. If the budget is exceeded, the producer trims wording rather than raising the budget.
Re-running the steward job, or giving the steward a model call, is a separate request.

acceptance_criteria.text: crates/athena-context/prompts/verifier.md says that when the request cites a document (a file or section), the verifier reads that document and compares the change with it, and that falling short of it is a request_reading_mismatch.

The producer or verifier prompt says a job may not mark its own requirement rows Covered, and the verifier flags any such change in docs/design/requirements-map.md as at least a major finding. Where a rule is prose-only, docs/enforcement.md or the decision entry says so.

In docs/design/requirements-map.md, rows A9-1 and A10-1 read Partial, each with the reason. A10-1: cost and yield tracking, reshaping and retiring are not built. A9-1: it names the cause for which the cell must say what is missing, namely that the steward never calls a model.
The G5 counts in docs/design/strategy-view.md match the map after the change, so a reader of the strategic view sees A9-1 and A10-1 as Partial, not Covered.
docs/decisions.md has a new entry with the alternatives and the tradeoff, citing job 20261014-174815-7bf8 as the case. CHANGELOG.md notes the change.
The token budgets still hold with the longer prompts. Run: cargo test --locked -p athena-cli --test budgets
The strategy view agrees with the map. Run: cargo test --locked --workspace
The workspace is clean. Run: cargo clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings, and cargo fmt --check

out_of_scope: Making the steward call a model
Building cost and yield tracking, reshaping or retiring of roles
Adding a second blind-spot source to the steward
Changing the verifier's scope rule on expected deliverables
Changing the code of judge() or the gate
